facility_roles.quote: The CHARM (CERN, Hamburg, Amsterdam, Rome, Moscow) Collaboration started to operate his detector in 1978, taking data with the CERN SPS neutrino beam.

intervals.label: proposal accepted
intervals.note: Year precision; the end is the start of data taking. The accepting body was CERN's Experimental Physics (EP) Division.
intervals.quote: In 1977 the proposal of the CHARM Collaboration (CERN-Hamburg-Amsterdam-Rome-Moscow Collaboration) to study semi-leptonic neutral current processes and muon polarization produced in neutrino and antineutrino interactions was accepted by the Experimental Physics (EP) Division.

intervals.label: data taking (WA18)
intervals.note: Data taking began in 1978 and ran with the complete apparatus from 1979 until 3 September 1984. Dore (EPJ H 37, 2012) and the CERN Courier (27 November 1998: 'A year later the 100 t CHARM electronic detector became operational', after 1977) agree on 1978. The collaboration also ran WA65 (1980-82, prompt neutrino production) and PS181 (a PS oscillation experiment, from 1983); these are not separate Atlas records.
intervals.quote: WA18: The data-taking of this SPS experiment began in 1978. WA18 started running with the complete apparatus in 1979, and was completed on the 3rd September 1984.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: WA18 'was completed on the 3rd September 1984'.

name: CHARM
notes: The record is the neutrino experiment WA18 of the CHARM Collaboration, not the later CHARM II (experiment:charm-ii) and not the name's charm-quark physics. The CERN Archives file covers 'CHARM I and CHARM II'.
The CHARM detector was followed by CHARM II, a separate collaboration and detector; no source calls CHARM II a successor, so no lineage row is recorded.

physics_goals.value: Study semi-leptonic neutral-current processes and the polarisation of muons produced in neutrino and antineutrino interactions

summary.plain: A 100-tonne detector of marble plates and tracking tubes at CERN's SPS, running from 1978 to 1984, built to study the neutral-current weak force in neutrino collisions and the quark structure of the nucleon.
summary.technical: CERN-Hamburg-Amsterdam-Rome-Moscow experiment WA18: low-density, low-Z calorimeter of 78 marble plates with proportional-tube and scintillator planes, magnetised-iron frames and a muon spectrometer of magnetised iron toroids, optimised for neutral-current events in SPS narrow- and wide-band beams; results on structure functions, neutrino-electron scattering, beam dump, mu+ polarisation and the electroweak mixing angle.
